title: Old Earth Hills
dek: Prima’s hills on the Eovar road. Their history includes the named hold Kûn Ardaire and a separate harpy-cave expedition, with routes clearer than the full underground geography.

facts.Recorded sites: Kûn Ardaire; the separate harpy-cave mountain route
facts.Eovar road: Explicitly crosses the hills after the First Forest

body:
The Old Earth Hills are part of northeastern Prima. The Eovar road crosses them after leaving the First Forest. Their scrub, slopes and rocky approaches contain more than one recorded expedition site, including the four-pillar entrance to Kûn Ardaire and the separate mountain route to the harpy cave.

The road from the forest

The 2 May 2024 journey names the transition plainly: Pristinia’s Eovar road skirts the First Forest, then enters the Old Earth Hills. Tall woodland gives way to shorter trees, shrubs and switchbacks. Later travelers use the same road while choosing whether to hunt or investigate beyond it.

These descriptions locate a route through the hills. They do not supply the hills’ full extent, a road to every ruin or a measured distance between all the places reached from Pristinia. The island map’s label north of The Before remains broad regional geography, not a plan of its caves.

The four-pillar ruins are Kûn Ardaire

The June company is led to the hills by Dale’s identification of the ruins. A landslide has exposed the cave, and the spectral keepers behind its four geometric pillars name the place Kûn Ardaire. The expedition enters old rooms and mines, then flees a creature from below and reseals the passage.

The later return supplies a second, direct location anchor. The narrator follows the road through the Old Earth Hills, identifies Olokun’s earlier entrance and describes the same pillars with a changed door. The scorched rooms and burned stair within preserve consequences of that first escape. Read the hold’s full exploration history →

19–27 September · the harpy cave

A different mountain route in the Old Earth Hills leads to the harpy cave. On the return, the company finds a narrow tunnel between great slabs of stone. It explains how the Matron’s song could travel beyond the nesting area, while leaving her reasons uncertain.

Inside are a corrupted body, violet reflections, altered creatures and eventually an unnamed dead person with a letter. The fragments do not form a clean sequence from oldest to newest, so their origin and movement cannot be reconstructed into one certain explanation. Moira’s proposed connection to The Before remains her theory.

Pell offers a last prayer before withdrawal. Saoirse’s Petalio strikes a weak support as the party leaves, collapsing the passage; the letter is taken to seek an identification. This changes that approach, rather than sealing every cave under the hills. Read the harpy expedition and its aftermath →

The eastern wilderness

The Alpine Forest’s regional opening places it beyond the hills to the east. Its cold woodland has its own narrated visits, remembered mine and fatal wolf encounter. The quarry expedition travels through the First Forest toward that direction before turning away in the foothills.

The evidence gives relative directions and separate experiences. It does not turn every mountain encounter into an Alpine Forest quest, put the quarry inside that forest or make the mine there part of Kûn Ardaire. Read the Alpine Forest’s exploration history →

Which expeditions can be placed here?

The strongest links come from named approaches, repeated entrances and descriptions of what changed on a return. The following connections retain those different levels of precision.

The four-pillar ruins — Kûn Ardaire in the Old Earth Hills; later narration identifies Olokun’s previous entrance.

The harpy cave — A separate mountain and descending tunnel explicitly in the hills; full connections underground remain unknown.

The quarry approach — Through the First Forest toward Alpine Forest, then off in the foothills. Its exact relationship to other hill sites is unrecovered.

The storm cave and other unnamed mountain episodes keep their broader Prima setting unless their own routes establish more. Similar rock, weather or underground scenery is not enough to merge them.

Connected histories The Before Survey · Quest Continuation · September–October 2026

A new landmark above the Gate road

The Twilight Observatory stands on a limestone cliff in the Old Earth Hills, visible from the route to the Gate. Its domes hold a telescope and an orrery; books and open-air terraces make room for learning. Aurélia opens its doors to Clive and Thorn, giving the hills a place where people can return to study as well as travel through.
